literal: Now you are demoted to Senior Concurrent Crown Prince Tutor; continue as Acting Regular Attendant and Minister as before, and one cycle of Regular Attendant stipend is stripped.
idiomatic: You are demoted to senior concurrent crown-prince tutor, your acting regular attendant and minister posts unchanged, with one year's regular-attendant stipend forfeited.

literal: He said to Left Vice Director Gongsun Liang and Right Vice Director Qifu Yishou: "The duty of the two vice directors is to assist and support the Masters of Writing, to illuminate intake and outflow; yet you could not set your hearts straight and speak plainly, to counsel and aid the Masters of Writing. Judging your offense, you should jointly face the death penalty.
idiomatic: He told Left Vice Director Gongsun Liang and Right Vice Director Qifu Yishou: "Your office exists to aid the Masters of Writing and keep the flow of documents clear; you failed to speak plainly and guide them. By rights you deserve death.

literal: But because the fault lay with the Masters of Writing and the matter centered on Shufan, separate demotion and punishment could not be imposed.
idiomatic: Because the Masters of Writing bore the blame and the affair turned on Shufan, he could not punish you separately.

literal: The two vice directors may in plain dress hold their original offices; caps, robes, stipends, and allowances are all stripped.
idiomatic: Both may keep their posts in plain dress, but caps, robes, stipends, and allowances are all taken away.

literal: If within three years there is achievement, restore the original posts;
idiomatic: If they prove themselves within three years, their posts may be restored;

literal: if there is no achievement, then forever return to the southern fields.
idiomatic: if not, they return forever to the fields.

literal: He also said to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Yuan Jing: "You yourselves took charge of the Collation Office and should have gathered up what was neglected and fallen away, yet you caused royal words to linger and daily records to go unrepaired—such guilt lies with you.
idiomatic: He told Regular Attendant Yuan Jing: "You were charged with the Collation Office and should have cleared its backlog, yet royal pronouncements stalled and the daily record fell into neglect—the fault is yours.

literal: Now demoted to Grand Master of the Palace and Acting Regular Attendant; one cycle of stipend stripped.
idiomatic: He was demoted to grand master of the palace and acting regular attendant, with one year's stipend cut.

literal: He said to Remonstrance and Counsel Grandee Li Yan: "Though you hold the remonstrance post, in truth you do not fit the office; you may leave remonstrance and withdraw as a gentleman of the first rank."
idiomatic: He told Remonstrance Grandee Li Yan: "You hold a remonstrance post but are unfit for it; leave remonstrance and withdraw as a gentleman of the first rank."

literal: He also said to Junior Mentor You Zhao and others: "Since Chenghua was established, a full year has passed, yet in the Eastern Palace there are no men who speak plainly; though three years have not yet passed, examination and dismissal are required."
idiomatic: He told Junior Mentor You Zhao and others: "Chenghua Palace has stood a year, yet the Eastern Palace still has no plain speakers; though three years are not up, they must be reviewed and culled."

literal: Zhao and Junior Household Master Li Ping have learning worth viewing and may be rated middle;
idiomatic: Zhao and junior household master Li Ping showed learning worth keeping and were rated middle;

literal: [11] Prince of Anle Quan may be rated lower-middle; release his Eastern Palace duty and withdraw as supernumerary Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry;
idiomatic: [11] Prince of Anle Quan was rated lower-middle, relieved of Eastern Palace duty, and made supernumerary regular attendant of scattered cavalry;

literal: Feng Su may be rated lowest; remove Junior Mentor, strip two ranks of nobility, supernumerary regular attendant as before;
idiomatic: Feng Su was rated lowest, removed as junior mentor and stripped two noble ranks, remaining supernumerary regular attendant;

literal: Junior Household Master Lü Xianbao may be rated lowest; withdraw as Martial Riding Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: Junior household master Lü Xianbao was rated lowest and made martial riding regular attendant.

literal: He also said to Gongsun Liang: "In recent years in appointing men, many appointments have violated judging talent and granting office.
idiomatic: He told Gongsun Liang: "Recent appointments have often ignored talent and fit.

literal: They were in truth military men yet given civil offices; dismissal follows the great precedent, yet in reason it is not even.
idiomatic: Military men were given civil posts; dismissing them by the general rule was not fair.

literal: For all cases like this, demotion of office returns to the original."
idiomatic: In every such case, offices were restored to what they had been."

literal: Gaozu summoned Lu Rui, Yuan Zan, and others before him and said: "Northerners always say, 'What use are books to northerners?' When I heard this I was deeply troubled.
idiomatic: Gaozu called Lu Rui, Yuan Zan, and others before him and said: "Northerners always ask what use books are to northerners; the remark troubled me deeply.

literal: Now those who know books are very many—are they all sages?
idiomatic: Many northerners read now; are they all sages?

literal: I myself have practiced ritual nine years and established offices three years, precisely intending to guide the myriad people and bring them to ritual teaching.
idiomatic: I have practiced ritual nine years and set offices three years, precisely to guide the people into ritual.

literal: I am Son of Heaven—why should I borrow the Central Plains? I wish your sons and grandsons to see broadly and know much.
idiomatic: I am Son of Heaven; why borrow the Central Plains? I want your sons and grandsons to see far and know much.

literal: If they forever dwell in the constant north and meet an unlettered lord, your sons and grandsons will not escape facing the wall.
idiomatic: If they stay forever in the north under a lord who scorns letters, your descendants will stand ignorant as men facing a wall.

literal: Lu Rui replied: "It is truly as the enlightened edict says: if the Jin clan had not entered Han office, renown through seven generations would also have been unobtainable."
idiomatic: Lu Rui replied: "It is as Your Majesty says: had the Jin clan never served Han, seven generations of fame would never have come."

literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased.
idiomatic: Gaozu was greatly pleased.

literal: When the five ranks were first established, Yu received a fief of two thousand households east of Dongguang in Bohai.
idiomatic: When the five ranks were opened, Yu's fief was two thousand households east of Dongguang in Bohai.

literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, Yu was advanced to Guard General,[12] appointed Bearer of the Staff, Controller of All Military Affairs of Qing, Qi, Guang, Nanqing, and the four provinces, Grand General Who Pacifies the East, with an open office, and Inspector of Qing Province.
idiomatic: On the southern campaign Yu was made guard general,[12] bearer of the staff, commander of Qing, Qi, Guang, Nanqing, and the four provinces, grand general who pacifies the east with an open office, and Qingzhou inspector.

literal: For merit in remaining to guard in place of the capital, his fief was increased by five hundred households.
idiomatic: For guarding the capital in the emperor's absence his fief rose by five hundred households.

literal: Gaozu visited Yu's residence and said to the younger princes: "Yesterday I personally received lawsuits and first learned how clear-sighted Guangling is."
idiomatic: Gaozu visited Yu's house and told the younger princes: "Yesterday I heard suits in person and first saw how clear-sighted Guangling is."

literal: Prince of Xianyang Xi replied: "In years I am Guangling's elder brother; in clarity I am Guangling's younger brother."
idiomatic: Prince Xianyang Xi replied: "I am older than Guangling in years but younger in clarity."

literal: Gaozu said: "I am your elder brother; you are Yu's peers—what further grievance have you?"
idiomatic: Gaozu said: "I am your elder brother and you are Yu's peers—what grievance remains?"

literal: He also said: "Shufan's deep illness dragged on for a full year; I was always deeply worried, fearing he would not recover.
idiomatic: He added: "Shufan's grave illness lasted a year; I feared constantly he would not rally.

literal: Now he has recovered and at last married—besides rejoicing in his good fortune, I ordered the carriage for that reason alone."
idiomatic: Now he is healed and newly wed; I came chiefly to share his joy."

literal: Gaozu personally saw him off at the Pavilion of the Imperial Grove.
idiomatic: Gaozu saw him off in person at the Pavilion of the Imperial Grove.

literal: Later an edict to Yu said: "I, by Heaven's calendar and fortune, seized the time and raised achievement, opened Jing and extended Mian, and my might shook Chu and Yue.
idiomatic: Later he edicted Yu: "By Heaven's calendar I seized the hour, opened Jing, extended Mian, and shook Chu and Yue.

literal: When the three flames came together I rested the carriage at Ru and Ying.
idiomatic: When the three flames aligned I halted at Ru and Ying.

literal: Power pressed Jing and Xu and sound blocked lands beyond the river; I could not yet lay aside armor when triumph entered the Three Rivers.
idiomatic: Power pressed Jing and Xu and sound blocked the lands beyond the river; armor could not yet come off when triumph was to enter the Three Rivers.

literal: I gather troops and repair statutes, waiting for autumn to raise the banner.
idiomatic: I gather troops and mend statutes, waiting for autumn to march.

literal: The charge over the eastern sea is therefore entrusted only to a clansman of merit; open the classics well and settle our eastern summer.
idiomatic: The eastern coast is entrusted to you alone as a worthy clansman; master the classics and settle our eastern realm.

literal: Be reverent and careful in your conduct; do not fall from fine repute; only wine, only fields—can they go unguarded!"
idiomatic: Keep your conduct reverent; do not lose your good name; guard against wine and idle fields!"

literal: He was made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and advanced to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry; the rest as before.
idiomatic: He was made regular attendant of scattered cavalry and grand general of chariots and cavalry; the rest unchanged.

literal: When Shizong took the throne he was transferred to Governor of Si Province, regular attendant as before.
idiomatic: At Shizong's accession he became Si province governor, regular attendant unchanged.

literal: Yu repeatedly memorialized to decline the governorship, reaching three or four times; edicts did not permit it.
idiomatic: Yu memorialized three or four times to resign the governorship; the throne refused.

literal: When Shizong took charge of government he summoned Yu within and in person appointed him Minister of Education.
idiomatic: When Shizong assumed government he brought Yu inside and named him minister of education in person.

literal: Yu declined, saying: "Yanhe from the first did not wish it, yet Your Majesty forced it upon him.
idiomatic: Yu declined: "Yanhe never wanted the post, yet Your Majesty forced it on him.

literal: Now he has just left that office and Your Majesty replaces him with me—certainly it will draw public criticism.
idiomatic: He has only just left it and Your Majesty would put me in his place—public talk is certain.

literal: Jiyu has already been transferred; taking it would be without suspicion.
idiomatic: Jiyu has already moved on; for me to take it would raise no suspicion.

literal: I ask to be made Minister of Works instead."
idiomatic: Let me be minister of works instead."

literal: Shizong still pressed him; when he firmly declined, permission was granted.
idiomatic: Shizong still pressed him; when Yu held firm, he was allowed his wish.

literal: Yu had earlier debauched the wife of supernumerary gentleman Feng Junxing; by night he went on a private visit and was struck by Junxing.
idiomatic: Yu had earlier debauched supernumerary gentleman Feng Junxing's wife; visiting her by night he was beaten by Junxing.

literal: For days he kept it secret; he died in his residence at thirty-two.
idiomatic: He hid the matter for days and died in his residence at thirty-two.

literal: Shizong came in person, grieving deeply; an edict granted the Eastern Garden warm-bright secret coffin, one set of court robes, one suit of garments, six hundred thousand cash, one thousand bolts of cloth, three hundred jin of wax, and the Grand Herald to oversee the funeral.
idiomatic: Shizong came in person, stricken with grief; the edict granted the eastern-garden secret coffin, court robes, a suit of garments, six hundred thousand cash, a thousand bolts of cloth, three hundred jin of wax, and the grand herald to direct the rites.

literal: At the great encoffment the emperor came in person and raised lament at the Capital Pavilion.
idiomatic: At the great encoffment the emperor came in person and mourned at the Capital Pavilion.

literal: Posthumously made Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Duke of Education, and Inspector of Ji Province; granted feather-canopy, drums, and pipes, and forty guards with ceremonial swords; posthumous title Hui.
idiomatic: He was posthumously bearer of the staff, palace attendant, grand general of agile cavalry, duke of education, and Jizhou inspector, with feather-canopy escort, drums, pipes, and forty ceremonial sword-guards; posthumous name Hui.

literal: At the burial the emperor came in person to see him off.
idiomatic: At the burial the emperor saw him off in person.

literal: His son Gong inherited.
idiomatic: His son Gong succeeded.

literal: The account is in the Annals.
idiomatic: The account appears in the Annals.

literal: Gong's elder brother Xin, style Qingle.
idiomatic: Gong's elder brother Xin, styled Qingle.

literal: By nature coarse and rash; he loved hawks and dogs.
idiomatic: Coarse and rash by nature, he loved hawking and hunting.

literal: At the beginning of Suzong's reign he was made Regular Attendant of Direct Transmission and General of the Northern Center.
idiomatic: Early in Suzong's reign he was regular attendant of direct transmission and general of the northern center.

literal: He went out as Champion General and Inspector of Jing Province, then transferred to General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Inspector of Qi Province.
idiomatic: He went out as champion general and Jingzhou inspector, then became general who subdues the barbarians and Qizhou inspector.

literal: In the two provinces Xin largely won men's hearts.
idiomatic: In both provinces Xin largely won popular attachment.

literal: He was again made General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Minister of the Household.
idiomatic: He was again made general who pacifies the east and grand minister of the household.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuang's reign he was enfeoffed Prince of Pei commandery with a fief of one thousand households; later changed to Prince of Huaiyang.
idiomatic: At Emperor Zhuang's accession he was made Prince of Pei commandery with a thousand households, later transferred to Huaiyang.

literal: In the time of the Deposed Emperor he was made Grand Mentor with an open office.
idiomatic: Under the Deposed Emperor he was made grand mentor with an open office.

literal: He was again enfeoffed Prince of Guangling.
idiomatic: He was again enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling.

literal: He was made Grand Tutor and Governor of Si Province, then soon removed as Grand Marshal.
idiomatic: He was made grand tutor and Si province governor, then soon grand marshal.

literal: He followed the Deposed Emperor and perished in Guanzhong.
idiomatic: He followed the Deposed Emperor and perished in Guanzhong.

literal: Prince of Gaoyang Yong, style Simu, in youth was unconstrained and unsteady.
idiomatic: Prince Gaoyang Yong, styled Simu, was in youth unconstrained and unsteady.

literal: Gaozu said: "I too cannot measure this child's depth; yet seeing his plain truth and unadorned simplicity, perhaps his vessel will ripen late."
idiomatic: Gaozu said: "I cannot plumb this boy's depth, but his plain truth suggests a late-blooming vessel."

literal: In the ninth year of Taihe he was enfeoffed Prince of Yingchuan, with Palace Attendant and Grand General Who Pacifies the South added.
idiomatic: In Taihe year 9 he was made Prince of Yingchuan, with palace attendant and grand general who pacifies the south.

literal: Someone urged Yong: "All the princes treat scholars to build reputation—why does Your Highness alone refuse?"
idiomatic: Someone urged Yong: "Other princes patronize scholars for renown—why do you alone refuse?"

literal: Yong said: "I am the Son of Heaven's son and stand among the princes—what need have I for reputation?"
idiomatic: Yong said: "I am the emperor's son and a prince among princes—what need have I of reputation?"

literal: After a long while he was appointed Central Guard and concurrently Grand General Who Guards the North.
idiomatic: After long service he was central guard and concurrently grand general who guards the north.

literal: His fief was changed to Gaoyang.
idiomatic: His fief was changed to Gaoyang.

literal: He was charged to convey the seven temples' spirit tablets to Luoyang.
idiomatic: He conveyed the seven temples' spirit tablets to Luoyang.

literal: When the five ranks were established, his fief was two thousand households.
idiomatic: When the five ranks opened, his fief was two thousand households.

literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, Yong acted as Grand General of the Garrison Army and held overall charge of affairs left behind.
idiomatic: On the southern campaign Yong was grand general of the garrison army and held overall charge of the capital.

literal: He was transferred to Commandant of the Guard, with Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry added, and appointed Bearer of the Staff, Grand General Who Guards the North, and Inspector of Xiang Province, regular attendant as before.
idiomatic: He became commandant of the guard and regular attendant of scattered cavalry, bearer of the staff, grand general who guards the north, and Xiangzhou inspector.

literal: Gaozu admonished Yong: "Xiang Province is the old capital; unless a court worthy of virtue and renown, none should dwell there—therefore I send you as governor.
idiomatic: Gaozu warned Yong: "Xiangzhou is the old capital; only a court worthy of virtue should hold it—hence I send you as governor.

literal: The way of governing is both hard and easy.
idiomatic: Governing is both hard and easy.

literal: [13] If the person is upright, without issuing orders things are done—therefore it is easy.
idiomatic: [13] If you are upright, things proceed without commands—that is the easy part.

literal: If the person is not upright, though orders are issued none follow—therefore it is hard.
idiomatic: If you are not upright, orders go unheeded—that is the hard part.

literal: You must also cherish worthy scholars, keep faith and covenants, and not lightly grant or strip office on others' words alone."
idiomatic: Cherish worthy men, keep faith, and do not grant or strip office lightly on hearsay."

literal: He was advanced to Grand General Who Pacifies the North.
idiomatic: He was advanced to grand general who pacifies the north.

literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Controller of All Military Affairs of Ji, Xiang, and Ying provinces, Grand General Who Pacifies the North, with an open office, and Inspector of Ji Province, regular attendant as before.
idiomatic: Early in Shizong's reign he was bearer of the staff, commander of Ji, Xiang, and Ying, grand general who pacifies the north with an open office, and Jizhou inspector.

literal: In the two provinces Yong had slight reputation.
idiomatic: In both provinces Yong won a modest name.

literal: He entered court as Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Si Province.
idiomatic: He entered court as grand general of agile cavalry and Si province governor.

literal: When Shizong visited Yong's residence he was treated with full family rites.
idiomatic: When Shizong visited Yong's house he was received with full family ceremony.

literal: He was transferred to Duke of Works and, in deliberating on statutes, Yong often entered to join the great deliberations.
idiomatic: He became duke of works and often joined the great deliberations on law.

literal: He was transferred to Duke of the Martial Host and Palace Attendant added.
idiomatic: He was made duke of the martial host with palace attendant added.

literal: At that time because of drought Yong twice memorialized to yield his post; gracious edicts did not permit it.
idiomatic: During drought he twice asked to resign; gracious edicts refused.

literal: He was made Grand Mentor, holding the Duke of the Martial Host concurrently, palace attendant as before.
idiomatic: He was made grand mentor while retaining the duke of the martial host, palace attendant unchanged.

literal: When Shizong carried out the method of examination and promotion, Yong memorialized:
idiomatic: When Shizong enacted examination and promotion, Yong memorialized:

literal: I venture to consider that examination every three years is the universal canon of the hundred kings.
idiomatic: I venture that triennial examination is the universal canon of kings.

literal: Now those in active office rated upper-middle advance one grade in three years; those among scattered offices rated top grade advance one rank in four years.
idiomatic: Active officers rated upper-middle now rise one grade in three years; top-rated scattered officers rise one rank in four.

literal: Idle and redundant offices were originally not vainly placed—some entered by talent and ability, some by accumulated diligence.
idiomatic: Idle posts were not vainly created—some men entered by talent, some by long service.

literal: If they lack ability they should not disgrace this high selection.
idiomatic: The unfit should not hold such high selection.

literal: Since they entered the court ranks by ability, some hold office on distant garrisons,[14] envoys to far borders, pressing for overdue taxes, inspecting provinces and garrisons—all are scattered offices filling arduous missions.
idiomatic: Men who entered by merit now serve on distant garrisons,[14] as envoys to far borders, pressing arrears, inspecting provinces—all scattered officers on arduous missions.

literal: Yet at examination and promotion they are ranked with the idle cohort.
idiomatic: Yet at examination they are ranked with the idle.

literal: To examine scattered officers—not all are inferior in talent; those who fit their tasks are not necessarily all worthy.
idiomatic: Among scattered officers talent is not uniformly low, nor are all who merely fill their posts worthy.
